identity.title: <SUP>13</SUP>CO/C<SUP>18</SUP>O Gradients across the Disks of Nearby Spiral Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use the IRAM Large Program EMPIRE and new high-resolution ALMA data to measure $^{13}$CO(1-0)/C$^{18}$O(1-0) intensity ratios across nine nearby spiral galaxies.

question.value: How does the 13CO/C18O (1-0) intensity ratio vary across the disks of nearby spiral galaxies, and what drives the variations (abundance vs optical depth)?

evidence.quote: Comparing transitions of different optically thin isotopologues, e.g., $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O, offers the chance to trace abundance variations across the disks of galaxies.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00004.SV.
with rest frequencies of 110.20 and 109.78 GHz
with rest frequencies of 110.20 and 109.78 GHz

angular_resolution.value: ALMA cubes convolved to 8"; EMPIRE at 33"

evidence.quote: For this letter, we use versions of these cubes convolved to 8$\ensuremath{''}$.

sensitivity.value: EMPIRE typical rms ~2.0 mK (Tmb) at 33" with 4 km/s channels

evidence.quote: At $33\ensuremath{''}$ resolution with $4$ km s$^{-1}$ wide channels, the typical rms noise is $\sim2.0$ mK ($T_{mb}$).

provided.value: 13CO and C18O maps of eight galaxies

evidence.quote: EMPIRE (cite: 2016ApJ...822L..26B) is mapping a suite of molecular lines across the whole area of nine nearby galaxy disks using the IRAM 30-m telescope.

provided.value: 12CO(2-1) used for local mean velocity for stacking

evidence.quote: we estimate the local mean velocity of gas from bright $^{12}$CO (2-1) emission from HERACLES (cite: 2009AJ....137.4670L).

provided.value: 70, 160, 250 micron maps for TIR / SFR surface density

evidence.quote: we combine $\lambda = 70$, 160, and 250$\mu$m maps from *Herschel* (cite: 2011PASP..123.1347K).

what.value: Sigma_SFR values from Leroy et al. 2013
Literature 13CO/C18O ratios for Milky Way, starbursts, ULIRGs

evidence.quote: Table [2](#table:results) includes a compilation of literature measurements targeting the central regions of starburst galaxies and ULIRGs.

array_combination.value: ALMA cubes feathered with IRAM for overlapping galaxies

evidence.quote: Those that overlap EMPIRE have been corrected to account for short and zero spacing information using the `CASA` task `feather`
we use versions of these cubes convolved to 8$\ensuremath{''}$.
for more details, see Gallagher et al. (in prep.).
(cite: 2016ApJ...822L..26B) describe the basic EMPIRE observation and reduction strategy.
we follow a procedure similar to that of (cite: 2011AJ....142...37S) and (cite: 2013AJ....146..150C)

unstated_but_needed: ALMA array configurations, dates, spectral setup, time on source
radial/IR zone definitions and bin edges

method.value: Divide galaxies into zones of radius or IR brightness, recenter spectra on local 12CO(2-1) mean velocity (13CO for ALMA C18O), average

evidence.quote: We recenter the $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O spectra about this local mean $^{12}$CO velocity. Then, we average all spectra in each zone to construct a single, high signal-to-noise spectrum.

method.value: Sum channels with bright 12CO(2-1) emission, window usually ~60 km/s; uncertainty from signal-free noise

evidence.quote: We calculated the uncertainty in the integrated intensity based on the noise estimated from the signal-free part of the stacked spectrum and the width of the integration window (usually $\sim$60 km s$^{-1}$).

method.value: TIR from Herschel 70/160/250 micron following Galametz et al. 2013, converted with Murphy et al. 2011

evidence.quote: calculate the TIR surface brightness following (cite: 2013MNRAS.431.1956G), and then convert to star formation rate surface density using the prescription of (cite: 2011ApJ...737...67M).

method.value: 13CO/12CO ratio assuming thick 12CO, common Tex and filling factor, CO(2-1) thermalized with (1-0)

used_for.value: feather to combine ALMA with short/zero spacing

evidence.quote: using the `CASA` task `feather`
We reduce the data using the GILDAS/CLASS software
using `DESPOTIC` (cite: 2014MNRAS.437.1662K)
The average $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O ratio for the inner $30\ensuremath{''}$ region of our targets is 6.0$\pm$0.9
we find a mean ratio of 7.9$\pm$0.8 for the whole galaxy disks
we find $0.05<\tau_{\rm13CO}<0.25$

findings_qualitative.value: Ratio increases with galactocentric radius and decreases with SFR surface density; NGC 628 is an outlier

evidence.quote: Leaving aside NGC 628, our targets tend to show rising $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O with increasing galactocentric radius and falling $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O with increasing $\Sigma_{\rm SFR}$.

claims.hypothesis: Normal spiral galaxies have central 13CO/C18O like the Milky Way rather than starbursts
claims.experiment: Stacked IRAM and ALMA spectra in the inner 30"
claims.result: 6.0±0.9 versus 3.4±0.9 for starbursts and 1.1±0.4 for ULIRGs

evidence.quote: This agrees well with results in the Milky Way, but differs from results for starburst galaxies (3.4$\pm$0.9) and ultraluminous infrared galaxies (1.1$\pm$0.4).

claims.hypothesis: Optical depth drives the ratio trends
claims.finding: Optical depth unlikely to drive trends; abundance changes preferred

evidence.quote: We argue that $^{13}$CO optical depth is unlikely to drive our observed trends.
We can therefore discard the possibility of selective photodissociation as an explanation for our results.

limitations_admitted.value: Nucleosynthesis not a general explanation given the Milky Way 12C/13C trend

evidence.quote: This argues against nucleosynthesis as a general explanation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Disentangling fractionation from nucleosynthesis needs more lines
ALMA sample is small and its processing is deferred to a companion paper
